content: The clinical condition known as hypothyroidism is primarily characterized by a reduced production of thyroid hormones. According to Chinese philosophical and medical theory, this condition is attributed to a deficiency in Yang energy. Chinese herbal medicines (CHM) are believed to restore Yang and have been traditionally used in China for the treatment of hypothyroidism over many years. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effects of CHM in the treatment of hypothyroidism. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across several databases, including The Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database on Disc, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure. The search for randomized clinical trials (RCTs) was completed in September 2014 for all databases. Additionally, trial registries were reviewed to identify any ongoing studies. The inclusion criteria for this review required RCTs that investigated CHM either as a standalone treatment or in combination with thyroid hormone therapy. These were compared against no treatment, placebo, or thyroid hormone therapy alone. The review also intended to compare different CHM formulations, either alone or in combination with thyroid hormone therapy. Participants in the studies were required to have a diagnosis of hypothyroidism based on the standard diagnostic criteria applicable at the time the trial began, regardless of the underlying cause of the condition. However, no RCTs meeting the inclusion criteria were identified. Consequently, data extraction and risk of bias assessment could not be performed. As a result, the effects of CHM on hypothyroidism could not be determined. In conclusion, there is currently no evidence from RCTs to support the use of CHM for the treatment of hypothyroidism. Furthermore, no ongoing registered trials investigating this topic were identified.
